iteration.area: Team DeliveryGate, TaskGraph scheduling, fullstack template migration, and ProductEval host validation
changes: Collect and deterministically bind the complete ChangeSet set for a task attempt into receipt evidence and a hash.
Keep TeamRun in AwaitingHuman and GoalRun in Verifying while required ChangeSets remain pending or conflicted.
Resume delivery after terminal ChangeSet decisions and idempotent accept replay, covering acceptance persisted before a process exit.
Reject or revert decisions close an impossible delivery as failed; restore conflicts remain recoverable in AwaitingHuman.
Publish successful TeamRun and ProjectSpace/manifest state atomically.
Extract receipt and ChangeSet delivery evidence helpers into workswarm/delivery_gate_evidence.rs.
Reject high/critical TaskGraph tasks unless a distinct independent review-capable role is available.
Bind independent reviewer steps to all high/critical task steps and make the final leader wait for those review steps.
Apply the dynamic TaskGraph before the next phase claims ready steps, including recovery after a succeeded lead.
On a fresh parallel run, execute the lead alone first; persist the dynamic task graph before dispatching workers.

Skip the fixed leader model step for independent dynamic task graphs and publish the host-validated artifacts via the DeliveryGate manifest; retain leader execution when task dependencies, overlapping write scopes, or shared contract references require integration.
Host DeliveryGate re-deserializes structured ReviewResult and rejects malformed findings, hidden blocker findings, or non-approved verdicts instead of relying only on the worker-side parser.

DeliveryGate now enforces reviewer capability ↔ review artifact kind, preventing a reviewer from bypassing structured ReviewResult checks by submitting a markdown/code artifact; non-review roles cannot label output as review evidence.

Delivery manifest now separates user-facing artifacts from review evidence: review artifacts remain indexed and represented in acceptance receipts but are excluded from manifest.artifacts and template evidence.
ProductEval fullstack Team now runs fixed file and command checkers before DeliveryGate finalization; failed checks rework the scoped producer or integrator within the existing retry budget.
After an integrator repair, the independent reviewer is explicitly reworked before validation and delivery, preventing reuse of a review from before the repair.
Host check results are reused by the outer ProductEval runner, avoiding a second command_check execution after accepted delivery.
Expected files are snapshotted before and after host validation; missing, unsafe, or changed files prevent acceptance.
TeamCoordinator now persists a host validation rejection as TeamRun Failed before delivery commit; an already committed Succeeded delivery cannot be revoked.
Automatic checker rework is audited as host_validator rather than attributed to the user.

Dynamic task assignment now binds project_integrator to every generated task step, including second and later tasks on a reused worker slot; leader remains bound to every task plus high-risk reviewers.
RunMeta now enables dynamic assignment when the resolved role list contains lead, covering selected templates whose lead role is only known after template expansion.
Migrate fullstack_web_v1 to lead plus bounded w1/w2 writer slots, a shared-surface project_integrator, and a read-only reviewer.
Preserve dynamic TaskGraph task acceptance/verification and the template handoff constraints in task-scoped worker prompts.
Bind every dynamic task, including additional tasks on reused worker slots, to integrator and reviewer prerequisites; require reviewers for high/critical tasks before leader finalization.
Keep legacy frontend_engineer/backend_engineer fullstack prompt aliases role-neutral while new templates use w1/w2.
Dynamic dependency rebinding now retains pre-existing template prerequisites for reviewer, project_integrator, and leader steps while adding every dynamic task edge.
ProductEval fullstack host-check repairs now target a dynamic task step using the failed path, assigned write scope, and latest matching ChangeSet; ambiguous owner evidence fails closed.
Dynamic host-check repair routing now rejects traversal paths and refuses role-level fallback when a dynamic owner has no task whose assigned write scope contains the failed file.

Add a bounded host-registered WorkspacePaths validator lane for file existence, non-empty content, required text, and top-level JSON field checks; reject traversal, reparse escapes, unsupported IDs/scopes, excessive resources, and oversized files.
Bind the project workspace root into TeamCoordinator before production WorkSwarm scheduling and bind ProductEval sandboxes for evaluation runs; absent or invalid host bindings fail closed.

Allow dynamic TaskGraph verification plans only through structured VerificationPlanV1 with host-derived IDs, registered WorkspacePaths validators, task write-scope containment, and bounded resources; do not execute model-selected commands.
Include verified workspace file hashes in DeliveryGate receipt subject hashes, evidence references, and receipt identity.

Execute host-bound WorkspacePaths validators inside GoalRunner before marking a step successful; persist per-step receipts with file hashes and keep dependency steps pending until required validation passes.

Reconnected ProductEval fullstack host validation before DeliveryGate finalization; host checker failures route to the latest successful dynamic task for the primary writer in the declared file scope, with command checks assigned to project_integrator.
Skip ProductEval Team local retry only for provider HTTP 429 code 1113 (insufficient balance/resource package); keep retries for transient rate limits.

Centralize provider non-retryable classification in the core gateway: HTTP 429 code 1113 stops gateway retries and fallback amplification; ProductEval consumes the same classifier while transient 429 remains retryable.

ProductEval now records executor, host-validation, and DeliveryGate wall time per run and reports stage means in aggregate and mode statistics; WorkSwarm records host-check and DeliveryGate elapsed time.

CLI statistics now render mean executor, host-validation, and DeliveryGate wall times; the summary explains that Team validation and gate timings overlap executor wall time, so total wall_ms remains the comparison metric.

Server DeliveryGate finalization now holds the workspace-global lease shared with Team writers across runtime completion, resumed ChangeSet acceptance, and ChangeSet restore; this closes the in-process check-to-publish write race.

Add DeliveryGate regression proving an earlier Passed receipt cannot authorize a changed final workspace file: the gate revalidates, writes a Failed receipt bound to the tampered file hash, and refuses TeamRun success.

iteration_notes: A regression assertion initially exposed that sorting before step identity binding reassigned the first worker task to a different task. The implementation was corrected to bind step IDs in source order and sort only the plan entries; the final targeted test passed.

A fresh-run regression now records actual Worker roles invoked during the first phase; only lead executes, while the dynamic task assignment is persisted for subsequent dispatch. The targeted test passed, then the full WorkSwarm integration suite passed 41/41.

The first independent-task test run showed GoalRunner can activate leader within the same phase after writers complete; the skip therefore moved into its host step-skipper. A follow-up exposed that the lead planning artifact is also accepted and listed in the manifest; the test now verifies writer producers and receipt/artifact parity rather than assuming only two manifest entries. Final WorkSwarm suite passed 42/42.

A permanent provider-resource failure was being retried inside ResilientProvider even after ProductEval skipped the outer Team retry. The core gateway now classifies code 1113 as non-retryable; the regression proves one outbound attempt while transient 429 still retries. No live speed claim follows from this request-count test.

The independent dynamic-task detector does not itself prove behavior acceptance. Production dynamic VerificationPlan currently permits only bounded WorkspacePaths checks, while the fullstack integrator owns command/test repair. Therefore the fixed integrator cannot be skipped safely until a host-authorized command ValidationLane can produce version-bound receipts; current performance work retains that quality boundary.
